fleetMemory.LESSON: A green deploy is not evidence that the intended commit shipped. DigitalOcean resolved branch main to f776b4bf — a commit from BEFORE the merge — while reporting build=SUCCESS deploy=SUCCESS and going ACTIVE, and served the pre-fix CR-stripped assets (144003/127885 against the correct 145758/131149). Read services[0].source_commit_hash back on every deployment and do not trust the branch name in the spec. The deltas being exactly the CR counts (1755 and 3264) was the detail that named the mechanism.

DigitalOcean exposes HISTORICAL container stderr at GET /v2/apps/{id}/deployments/{dep}/logs?type=DEPLOY as a gzip-pressed signed URL in historic_urls. /logs?type=RUN refuses with 'cannot get running logs ... in phase final_cleanup' once the deployment is done. Decompress and read it: it turns 'your container exited with a non-zero exit code' into the actual stack trace, which is what named assertNoSupplierDsn. BUILD serves the same shape for build logs.

`gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=X --format=value(payload.data)` piped through a shell and base64-decoded is LOSSY. It returned 75 and 80 bytes of binary across two calls for a secret whose payload is 148 printable bytes containing postgres:// and neon.tech — and the two calls disagreed with each other, which is the tell. Use --out-file and read the file, then assert the shape you expect (this lane asserts a Neon DSN) before spending a deploy on it. Same family as the dispatch's own warning about positional gcloud formatters.

A product's own boot guard is a better oracle than an operator's assumption. smartcity-dashboards refuses any DATABASE_URL that is not postgres:// on neon.tech via assertNoSupplierDsn at src/mounts.mjs:121, which runs at import time in server.mjs — so a bad DSN is a hard boot failure, not a warning. When a container dies at boot with a config-sourced value, read the guard before suspecting the platform or the branch.

A non-production proof target built as a NEW app is not a faithful control for repointing an EXISTING app, because DigitalOcean secrets are APP-SCOPED: PUT of one app's EV[ENCRYPTED[...]] value into another app is rejected with 'secret env value cannot be decrypted'. Either re-supply plaintext at create time or prove the change on the app itself; the UAT app and dolphin-app could only be compared at the branch and payload layer, not at the env layer.

GATE B needs the commit's own diff stat first. `git show --name-only f776b4bf` returning zero web/ files is what forced a behavioural marker (a 500 body) instead of a byte in a payload — and that marker then doubled as an origin discriminator for a Cloudflare-proxied hostname where edge headers cannot discriminate.
fleetMemory.DEAD-END: Do not try to make a non-production DigitalOcean app a faithful clone of an existing one by copying its env array from the API. All 10 values come back as EV[ENCRYPTED[...]] and the PUT is refused cross-app with 'secret env value cannot be decrypted'. The failure is immediate and safe (400, no change) but it costs a round trip; plan for re-supplying plaintext instead.

Do not read the DigitalOcean certificate or domain state to decide whether anything is working. app.smartcityos.io has no A record and adding it to the app would start ACME retries against a non-resolving name; the dispatch's own trap (a status field that stopped changing is not evidence a process stopped) applies to the domain field the same way it applies to a certificate field.
